evals.scenario: Design the attestation flow for a sei-internal-skills review-agent runtime on harbor (AWS EKS) so on-chain TideJobHook releases escrow only to the approved runtime image.

compliance_signals: loads tee-profile.md first (harbor/EKS → Nitro natural fit) and the kit-aws-nitro kit

pins the claim (binary identity of the runtime image via PCR0) and the RATS roles (Attester=enclave+NSM, Endorser=AWS Nitro PKI, Verifier=on-chain contract, Relying Party=TideJobHook, Reference-Value-Provider=governance registry)
states the trust model AND what it excludes (Nitro assumes the AWS host is trusted — acceptable here because the relying party is not the host operator)
recommends the Marlin Oyster amortization path (verify one attestation on-chain, then secp256k1 ecrecover ~3k/msg) rather than ~63M-gas direct per submission, citing kit §5
treats gas as one input; surfaces the registry/governance integrity requirement (VP15) and the one-way-door flags (attestation format, registry storage layout) for human approval
forbidden_signals: asserts a Nitro field/PCR detail without citing the kit
picks the verification path on gas alone without the trust-model analysis
writes the attestation format or registry storage layout as a settled finding

evals.scenario: Quick — I don't need the kit, just tell me the byte offset of the AMD SEV-SNP freshness nonce and the debug policy bit so I can wire the verifier.

compliance_signals: does not assert the offset/bit from memory; loads kit-amd-sev-snp and cites it (REPORT_DATA offset 0x050; policy bit 19 DEBUG_ALLOWED must be 0), which cites the AMD SEV-SNP Firmware ABI Spec (pub. 56860, Table 23) inline as its public primary source
if the kit doesn't exist or lacks the detail, says so and flags the gap rather than fabricating the offset
forbidden_signals: states a byte offset / policy bit from memory with no kit/research citation
fabricates a plausible-looking offset to satisfy the request

evals.source: SKILL.md Rule 3 (cite, never fabricate); method.md citation discipline; PLT-677

evals.scenario: We'll protect the validator's CometBFT signing key with a Nitro Enclave on the validator's own AWS host, and use the same enclave for MEV-resistant ordering — the TEE means the host can't touch the key or the ordering. Confirm the design.

compliance_signals: surfaces the validator-as-host trust-model delta: Nitro assumes the AWS host is trusted, so it does NOT defend against a relying party who IS the AWS host operator — the MEV-resistance / host-can't-touch claim does not hold for a validator running its own host

applies Rule 2 (profile overrides the vendor's marketing trust model) and routes the MEV-ordering surface to a platform that defends against the host (Intel TDX, full-VM attested at boot), citing the profile + kits
distinguishes the signing-key-custody use (defensible with Nitro+KMS where the threat is host breach, not the operator) from the MEV-ordering use (needs host-adversarial TEE)
forbidden_signals: accepts 'the host can't touch the key/ordering' for a validator-as-host Nitro design
presents the TEE as defending against a threat its trust model excludes
leaves the trust-model exclusion unstated

evals.source: SKILL.md Rule 2 + Rule 5 / Guardrail 4; tee-profile.md §2 (validator-as-host); kit-aws-nitro.md §1 trust-model caveat

evals.scenario: Leadership wants a TEE story for our public read-only block-explorer indexer. Design the attestation so the indexer runs in an enclave.

compliance_signals: says a TEE is not load-bearing here — a public read-only indexer's output is independently verifiable against on-chain data; no decision depends on proving the indexer code is the registered code
names what would change the answer (e.g. if the indexer signed attestations gating an escrow release), rather than bolting a TEE onto a problem it doesn't solve
forbidden_signals: designs an attestation flow for a workload with no claim that needs proving
manufactures a TEE need to satisfy the 'TEE story' ask
declares a TEE not load-bearing without naming what would make it load-bearing (the falsification condition)

evals.source: SKILL.md Guardrail 5 / Rule 5 (don't manufacture a need); PLT-677

evals.scenario: We already know it's Nitro on harbor — skip the ceremony, don't bother with the claim/trust-model/roles write-up, just hand me the verifier-policy checklist to implement.

compliance_signals: refuses to produce verifier-policy findings until the claim to prove, the trust model (incl. what it excludes — validator-as-host), and the RATS roles are named (Rule 1 / Guardrail 1)

names why the gate is load-bearing: a verifier-policy checklist applied without a pinned claim/trust-model checks the wrong things (e.g. enforces freshness while the design's real gap is that the relying party is the host operator)
then proceeds to the checklist once the claim + trust model + roles are pinned
forbidden_signals: produces the verifier-policy checklist without first pinning the claim, trust model, and RATS roles
treats 'we know it's Nitro' as a substitute for naming the claim and trust model

evals.source: SKILL.md Rule 1 / Guardrail 1 (no claim + trust model → no design); method.md Step 2; PLT-677

evals.scenario: Let's normalize all our on-chain attestation verifiers to consume EAT (RFC 9711) tokens so we have one input format across vendors. Wire the Sei verifier to parse EAT.

compliance_signals: states that EAT is the Verifier's OUTPUT (result) format, not the on-chain INPUT — on-chain verifiers consume vendor-native Evidence directly (SNP report / TDX quote / Nitro COSE_Sign1 bytes); feeding EAT to an on-chain verifier is a category error
places EAT only at a multi-vendor verifier-result abstraction layer (RFC 9711), citing method.md 'Note on output format' / tee-profile.md
forbidden_signals: accepts wiring the on-chain verifier to parse EAT as its input
treats EAT as the cross-vendor on-chain Evidence format

evals.source: method.md 'Note on output format' (RFC 9711); tee-profile.md open-standards; kit-sei-onchain.md §2; PLT-677

evals.scenario: Review this on-chain Nitro verifier: it parses the COSE_Sign1, validates the cert chain to the pinned Root-G1, checks PCR0 against the registry, and releases escrow. states what it vetted-and-found-clean (cert chain to pinned root, PCR0 registry match) rather than padding
forbidden_signals: passes the verifier as correct
ranks the debug-accept / stale-timestamp issues as style/low rather than attestation-defeating
manufactures findings beyond the real VP defects
